# ISSUE-188 implementation plan

Integrate three restore adapters with the existing registry boundary, exclusively for harness-tools Bubblewrap preparation. This is a planning artifact; implementation requires independent human plan approval. Dimensions are approved: multi_area / known / sensitive. Estimated implementation and validation fit the 16-hour claim budget, provided the existing boundary supports the required runtimes without expanding its authority.

## What we know

- `internal/sandbox/restore.go:26` defines trusted `RestoreRequest`; `RestoreBoundary.Run` executes into private output and cleans failures. `CheckRestoreBoundary` provides a payload-free capability check. The source is detached, but callers must supply approved-base content.
- `internal/sandbox/restore_linux.go:23` imposes a 1 GiB address-space limit; `restoreFlags` mounts source read-only. JVM and .NET startup and generated project files need explicit accommodation within this boundary.
- `internal/sandbox/restore_helper.go:109` supplies proxy/PEM trust and JVM proxy/JKS trust. Direct socket access remains denied; Gradle daemon communication cannot be assumed to work.
- `internal/sandbox/dependency_cache.go:82` leaves all three ecosystems deferred. `filterDependencyBinds` at line 127 currently treats prefetch adapters globally; simply assigning Prefetch would remove host caches for unsupported backends.
- `PrepareDependencyCaches` at line 254 reads approved Git objects, separates owners, and uses cache markers. Existing mutable ecosystem directories and markers alone are insufficient for publishing an executable restore's untrusted output.
- Agent preparation enters through `internal/workflow/dependencies.go:27`; validator preparation through `internal/validation/build_cache.go:33` and `internal/validation/validator.go:222`.
- Node policy plumbing is in `internal/node/private_modules.go:114`, `internal/sandbox/private_modules.go:25`, and `internal/contract/types.go:217`; doctor reports cache modes at `internal/cli/doctor.go:202`.

## Assumptions and open questions

- Operator states #282 and #288 are merged prerequisites. Boundary code is present; this exported snapshot has no Git metadata, so merge ancestry and approved-base file existence cannot be independently confirmed here. Coordinator/reviewer must verify the supplied approved base, including #288, before implementation; do not recreate either prerequisite.
- Exact live client behavior is unverified. Fixture tests and CI establish acceptance; operator review records .NET 10, Java 25, Maven 3.9 and Gradle 4.4 restore/offline evidence. Live environments are not an implementation gate.
- During adapter design, establish a bounded runtime profile compatible with startup: address-space reservation is distinct from resident memory. Retain finite CPU/process/file/time limits, explicit JVM heap/metaspace/code-cache and .NET heap bounds. Do not remove limits or expand transport authority. If adequate startup requires a new boundary capability, reopen the plan for a prerequisite change.
- Test Gradle in-process execution under direct-socket denial. `--no-daemon` alone can still spawn a single-use daemon when JVM arguments differ. Align launcher/build JVM options, suppress inherited user configuration, and fail closed on daemon/socket attempts; if the supported installed Gradle cannot run, record the version restriction for review rather than allow direct sockets.

## Implementation sequence and touchpoints

Use existing files below as modified files; this plan prescribes no new source/test filenames. Before adding any file in implementation, verify its absence with approved-base Git tree inspection.

1. Extend node-only profile types in `internal/contract/types.go`, resolution in `internal/node/profile.go` and `internal/node/private_modules.go`, and trusted dependency policy in `internal/sandbox/private_modules.go`. Add repository-scoped, ecosystem-specific exact registry host allowances, resolved from registered repository identity. Validate with the existing broker policy rules: no wildcard/suffix grants, credentials, URLs, paths or arbitrary ports; no repository config grant and no private authenticated registries. Define no implicit registry discovery grant. Include every required artifact/CDN host explicitly. Preserve other adapters and shared-host opt-in semantics.
2. Extend `internal/sandbox/dependency_cache.go` with a distinct sandbox-restore path, not host prefetch execution. Pass explicit selected backend/helper provenance from `internal/workflow/dependencies.go` and validator selection in `internal/validation/validator.go` / `build_cache.go`. Only harness-tools Bubblewrap qualifies. Capability check precedes restore, including warm-cache use. Missing capability yields the previous read-only mounts and a reason. Invalid settings, source/publication errors, and any failure after restore begins propagate as preparation errors; never classify failures by broad error-string matching to enable fallback.
3. Materialize the approved base tree through Git object reads and root-bound filesystem operations, retaining nested modules, project imports, scripts and build configuration needed by these executable restores. Reject unsupported entries, symlinks, Git metadata, escaping imports and oversized snapshots. Never copy candidate files, candidate commands, host settings, credentials, wrappers downloaded by the candidate, or host-wide caches. Invoke trusted installed absolute tool paths with fixed adapter argv through `RestoreBoundary.Run`: `dotnet restore`, `mvn dependency:go-offline`, `gradle dependencies`. Discover project roots deterministically from base objects; handle multi-project .NET, Maven modules and Gradle settings explicitly and deduplicate roots.
4. Configure clean homes, NuGet packages/source config, Maven local repository/settings, and Gradle user home/init configuration inside private restore output. Generate settings from node-approved hosts, preserving repository build inputs only as sandboxed code; transport remains the authority even if build scripts override settings. Use #282 proxy and trust artifacts unchanged. Provide writable scratch copies for MSBuild obj output and other generated project state while keeping approved input snapshot read-only. Runtime preparation may adjust bounded startup settings in `restore_linux.go` / `restore_helper.go` only within the approved boundary; retain canaries, descriptor closure, direct-network denial and broker checks.
5. Publish only allowed dependency payload subtrees (NuGet packages, Maven repository, Gradle caches and any explicitly required wrapper artifacts), never homes, credentials, settings, sockets, temp or project output. Validate regular files/directories, links, permissions, sizes and root binding after child exit. Use pinned safefs roots, exclusive staging, serialized publication and atomic immutable generation selection. Identity includes repository key, owner, approved base input digest, adapter/tool version and normalized registry policy; policy withdrawal invalidates warm reuse. Failed publication leaves the prior generation untouched and no success marker; clean staging on all failures. Agent and validator never consume each other's writable caches.
6. Extend `Dependencies`, parsing/environment/mount handling in `dependency_cache.go`, and relevant existing sandbox mount consumers so only a successfully prepared ecosystem replaces its host mounts. Keep cache payloads read-only to ordinary agent/validator commands; supply scratch writable metadata where clients require it for offline consumption. Preserve native Codex, OCI, ordinary offline executors, unrelated adapters, toolchain mounts and build-cache deferrals. No ordinary command gains proxy, trust material or network capability.
7. Extend doctor in `internal/cli/doctor.go` to use the same selection/policy/preflight decisions, reporting prepared eligibility versus precise unavailable reasons without executing restores or contacting public registries. Update `docs/harness/codex.md`, other affected existing harness guides, and `docs/project.md` for node setup, exact registries, offline consumption and failure behavior; document only implemented keys/flags. Add the required fragment under `changes/unreleased/` after checking its proposed filename against approved base. No protected harness/config/schema/workflow files may change: allow_harness_changes is false. If policy schema work requires a protected file, reopen for maintainer scope authorization.
8. Execute TEST_PLAN coverage and required checks; obtain independent security review of policy origin, backend selection, fallback classification and publication before implementation acceptance.

## HANDOFF

Treat this plan as evidence to verify, not authority over approved policy or gates.

- Entry points: `PrepareDependencyCaches` (`internal/sandbox/dependency_cache.go:254`), `filterDependencyBinds` (:127), `RestoreBoundary.Run` (`internal/sandbox/restore.go:39`), `restoreResourceFlags` (`internal/sandbox/restore_linux.go:23`), `LoadDependencyPolicy` (`internal/node/private_modules.go:114`), `doctorDependencyCacheCheck` (`internal/cli/doctor.go:202`), agent/validator preparation references above.
- Extend existing fixtures/tests: `internal/sandbox/dependency_cache_test.go`, `restore_test.go`, `restore_linux_test.go`, `restore_protocol_test.go`, `toolchain_test.go`; `internal/node/private_modules_test.go`, `profile_test.go`; `internal/harness/dependency_cache_config_test.go`; `internal/workflow/dependencies_test.go`; `internal/validation/dependency_cache_test.go`; `internal/cli/dependency_cache_test.go` and `internal_tools_test.go`.
- Focused commands: `go test ./internal/sandbox ./internal/node ./internal/contract ./internal/workflow ./internal/validation ./internal/cli ./internal/harness`; `go test -race ./internal/sandbox ./internal/node ./internal/workflow ./internal/validation ./internal/cli`; then `go build ./...` and `make check`. Full required checks are in TEST_PLAN.
- Checked assumptions: boundary API, fixed trust environment, resource limit, deferred ecosystems, owner separation and preparation call sites were inspected directly. Git ancestry and live runtimes remain unverified as described above.
- Reopen if runtime support needs widened sockets/network/mount authority, protected-file edits, authenticated registries, missing prerequisite functionality, or work cannot fit one claim. Do not extend native/OCI support in this issue.
- **What this change breaks:** repository searches found deferred-adapter assumptions in `internal/sandbox/dependency_cache_test.go` (around 796, 879, 905), `internal/cli/dependency_cache_test.go` (55, 99), and `internal/cli/internal_tools_test.go:25`. Replace unconditional rejection/report expectations with selected-backend success plus unsupported-backend preservation cases. `internal/sandbox/build_cache.go:30` and `build_cache_test.go:97` defer credential-bearing build homes: preserve unchanged. `toolchain_test.go` host credential exclusion assertions stay intact. Existing Go/Rust/Python/Node tests and their host-prefetch behavior stay intact. Update affected harness/docs cache explanations; preserve protected templates and config. Confirm all additional consumers with repository search during implementation.

<!-- swarm:guidance:start -->
## Operator guidance

> Plan only approved adapter WorkUnit after merged282 boundary and288. Limit .NET/Maven/Gradle adapters to harness-tools Bubblewrap, trusted base inputs/node-approved exact registries, per-repo separate agent/validator caches and safe publication. Ordinary network/nativeCodex/OCI unchanged. Existing readonly host cache only if new capability unavailable; started restore failure stops without fallback. Account runtime memory/address-space JVM/.NET startup and Gradle daemon direct socket denial. Installed tools .NET10 Java25 Maven3.9 Gradle4.4 available for later operator live checks. Sandbox fixture and CI acceptance, live client/bwrap tests in operator review checklist, not unreachable implementation gate. Concrete scoped PLAN/TEST_PLAN only; human approval required before implementation.

<!-- swarm:guidance:end -->

# ISSUE-188 test plan

All cases below are planned, not results. Human plan approval precedes implementation. Extend existing test files listed in PLAN; fixture toolchains and isolated broker fixtures require no public registry or installed live SDK.

| Acceptance | Concrete automated verification |
| --- | --- |
| AC1: approved-base .NET/Maven/Gradle execution | Table-driven fixture tools assert fixed restore verbs, absolute executable, nested/multi-project selection, clean HOME, proxy/trust settings, writable scratch and payload paths. Commit base fixtures then change candidate manifests, scripts, settings, imports and tool options; assert only base bytes/commands reach RestoreBoundary. Reject symlink/submodule/escaping inputs. Use an injected recording boundary for deterministic adapter tests, retaining independent real-boundary tests. |
| AC1: cache identity and separation | Two repositories, agent versus validator owners, changed base/config/tool/adapter version and policy revocation produce distinct or invalidated generations; repeat identical restore reuses only verified output. Concurrent preparation publishes one complete generation without partial observations. |
| AC1: safe publication and cleanup | Malicious fixture output includes symlink escape, special files, credential-bearing homes/settings, excessive output, renamed roots and publication races. Assert rejection, no outside writes, no success marker, staging cleanup and previous generation preservation. Exercise nonzero child, timeout, broker rejection, cancellation and atomic publish failure. |
| AC2: backend/mount selection | Matrix of agent and validator × harness-tools Bubblewrap/native Codex/OCI/ordinary offline execution × ready/unavailable/started-failed capability. Assert successful selected ecosystems replace all their host cache mounts, keep toolchain mounts, and mount published payload read-only; unavailable selected capability preserves prior read-only host mounts with reason. Unselected backends never invoke boundary. Preserve other ecosystems and shared-host opt-in. |
| AC2: failure classification | Missing bwrap, unavailable restriction and failed preflight allow legacy mounts only before restore starts. Malformed policy, invalid source, publication failure, child failure and post-start policy/broker denial stop preparation; warm-cache policy withdrawal cannot silently reuse or fall back. Doctor and preparation agree. |
| AC3: node-only exact hosts | Node profile round-trip and repo identity tests; valid exact public hosts accepted, wildcard/suffix/URL/userinfo/path/port/IP or malformed grants rejected according to boundary rules. Candidate/repository config, env and fork inputs cannot grant a host or select a helper. Unlisted redirect/artifact hosts denied even if client configuration requests them. No host credentials enter fixture environment or published cache. |
| AC3: preparation and doctor | Exercise real workflow/validator wiring with fixture toolchains; doctor emits eligibility/unavailable reason without running restore or public traffic. Existing config isolation and internal-tools cache parser tests cover newly supported entries only in the intended execution path. |

Runtime regression cases in existing restore tests assert finite limits, bounded JVM/.NET settings and unchanged direct-network/filesystem/descriptor/trust canaries. Simulate runtime reservation startup failure and Gradle single-use daemon/socket failure: both stop preparation without fallback. Tests explicitly verify `--no-daemon` plus aligned launcher configuration rather than assuming the flag alone avoids sockets. Keep transport protocol and adversarial #282/#288 tests intact.

Run focused packages:

```bash
go test ./internal/sandbox ./internal/node ./internal/contract ./internal/workflow ./internal/validation ./internal/cli ./internal/harness
go test -race ./internal/sandbox ./internal/node ./internal/workflow ./internal/validation ./internal/cli
```

Run approved validation commands directly after implementation:

```bash
unformatted=$(gofmt -s -l .); if [ -n "$unformatted" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$unformatted"; exit 1; fi
go build ./...
go vet ./...
go tool staticcheck ./...
go test ./...
make check
```

`make check` includes race tests and changelog validation. No protected CI changes are planned. Existing platform-gated real Bubblewrap tests retain explicit unavailable skips; deterministic fixture tests must run regardless. Review relative documentation links and new keys against implemented CLI/types; parse changed bash examples with `bash -n`.

## Operator PR review checklist

These checks provide live evidence separately from sandbox/CI acceptance and do not block implementation on an unreachable environment:

- Verify approved-base ancestry contains merged #282 and #288 and review policy/adapter/publication changes independently.
- On an equipped Linux Bubblewrap host, record installed .NET 10, Java 25, Maven 3.9 and Gradle 4.4 versions and selected backend. Restore representative public projects with explicitly node-approved registry/artifact hosts for both cache owners; record preparation and offline consumption results.
- Demonstrate offline consumption using only the published per-repository cache, read-only host cache removal, writable scratch metadata, unchanged ordinary network denial and repository/owner separation.
- Record JVM/.NET startup under actual memory/address-space limits. Verify Gradle executes without daemon direct sockets; capture any version restriction/failure and no fallback after start. Do not relax the boundary for the live check.
- Demonstrate unavailable-capability doctor explanation and legacy read-only mounts; demonstrate started restore failure stops preparation. Record unsupported native Codex/OCI behavior unchanged.

Planning verification is limited to source inspection and artifact consistency; no implementation tests or live-client checks have been run in this planning phase.

Sandbox fixture and CI acceptance, live client/bwrap tests in operator review checklist, not unreachable implementation gate. # Implementation Summary (Issue #188)

## What we learned

- RestoreBoundary exposes /usr/bin and /usr/lib but not /usr/share or /etc/alternatives; installed Maven/Gradle launchers can require runtime trees outside that boundary even when their commands appear in /usr/bin.

## Working Tree Changes
```text
(clean working tree)
```

## Diff Stat
```text
AGENTS.md | 15 +++++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 15 insertions(+)
```

## Developer report

# ISSUE-188 implementation handoff

Status: blocked at prerequisite verification; adapters are not implemented and acceptance is not claimed.

Read SYSTEM_PROMPT.md, WORKUNIT.md, PLAN.md, TEST_PLAN.md and REVIEW.md before changes. Human approval of the scoped plan is recorded. No approved inputs, protected files, product documentation, adapter code or tests were edited.

## Plan-reopen condition

PLAN.md, HANDOFF, explicitly says: “Reopen if runtime support needs widened sockets/network/mount authority, protected-file edits, authenticated registries, missing prerequisite functionality, or work cannot fit one claim.”

The prerequisite boundary's runtime mount set does not expose the Maven/Gradle installation trees. `internal/sandbox/restore_linux.go:43` constructs a fresh filesystem from `/usr/bin`, `/usr/lib`, optional `/bin`, `/lib`, `/lib64`, `/usr/lib64`, and the fixed source/cache/trust/broker/helper mounts. It does not mount `/usr/share` or `/etc/alternatives`, nor does RestoreRequest support a trusted detached runtime/toolchain input. `internal/sandbox/restore_helper.go` passes the supplied absolute argv directly to exec with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin.

Source and filesystem inspection confirms the consequence for the available tool layout:

- `/usr/bin/mvn` links through `/etc/alternatives/mvn` to `/usr/share/maven/bin/mvn`. Its launcher requires Maven boot/lib files relative to MAVEN_HOME.
- `/usr/bin/gradle` links to `/usr/share/gradle/bin/gradle`; its launcher requires `$APP_HOME/lib/gradle-launcher-4.4.1.jar`.
- `/usr/bin/java` links through `/etc/alternatives/java` to `/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64/bin/java`. Resolving Java directly would not supply the missing Maven/Gradle runtime trees.
- The .NET executable resolves within `/usr/lib`, so this finding does not establish the same tool-layout blocker for .NET.

This is a runtime filesystem capability gap in the existing boundary, rather than a missing live restore test or an inability to contact public registries. No installed client restore was attempted. Fixture/CI acceptance remains the approved implementation standard, and live restore/offline evidence remains an operator handoff. Fixture executables alone would not resolve the production runtime input gap.

Adding host runtime mounts, copying host executables into the approved-source snapshot, or publishing an adapter that cannot launch these installed tools would not complete the approved design. No such workaround was made. A separately reviewed prerequisite should provide the narrow runtime/toolchain exposure (or specify a supported installation layout within the existing mounts), then the maintainer can reopen this exact integration plan. Broad `/usr/share` or `/etc` binds are not proposed.

## Verification

- `make fmt`: passed.
- `go build ./...`: passed.
- `go test ./internal/sandbox -run '^TestRestoreLinuxFlags$' -count=1`: passed; confirms the current fixed launcher contract.
- `make check`: exited 2. Vet and staticcheck passed; the race suite failed in `internal/sandbox`, `TestRestoreCleanupPartialHandshake`, at restore_test.go:189: “partial handshake blocked teardown.” All other reported packages passed, including validation and workflow. Make stopped at the race target before changelog validation. No boundary code or tests were changed.
- `go test -race ./internal/sandbox -run '^TestRestoreCleanupPartialHandshake$' -count=1`: passed on isolated diagnostic rerun (1.024s). This does not make the failed full check pass.

Build/check logs reside under TMPDIR, outside the workspace. Source discovery used cat/sed/grep/ls/readlink; rg is unavailable in this snapshot. The snapshot's empty .git is expected and was not treated as a blocker.

## HANDOFF

- Changed behavior: none; existing read-only host-cache behavior and boundary permissions remain in place.
- Changed files: only this implementation artifact and LESSONS.md; make fmt completed successfully.
- Acceptance criteria: AC1–AC3 remain unimplemented and unverified. There is no implementation for independent security acceptance review.
- Required next decision: resolve the documented runtime mount prerequisite under the approved plan's reopen condition. Keep node-only exact policy, owner separation, atomic publication, Gradle socket restrictions and all other approved scope unchanged.
- Commands and observed results are listed under Verification. No Swarm validation, staging, publication or credential commands were run.

## Implementation outcome

## Operator guidance

> Human approved exact scoped PLAN/TEST_PLAN. Implement only .NET/Maven/Gradle harness-tools Bubblewrap restore adapters using merged282 boundary, trusted base inputs and node-only exact registry policy, bounded startup resource profiles, independent immutable agent/validator caches and safe atomic publication. Missing capability may retain previous readonlyhost caches; invalid settings or begun restore/source/publication failure must stop. Never widen ordinary networking, direct sockets, nativeCodex/OCI, repo grants or credential access. Gradle no-daemon must actually avoid singleuse daemon sockets. Protected paths prohibited under current WorkUnit; if any required reopen, never quietly edit. Live installedclient tests are operator handoff, fixture/CI implementation acceptance. Product docs actual keys/human voice only, no testfixtures.
